newsitem.title: USA: Excel acquiring Telco for $1 billion.
newsitem.headline: Excel acquiring Telco for $1 billion.

text.p: Excel Communications Inc. said Friday it has a definitive agreement to acquire Telco Communications Group Inc. for about $1 billion, solidifying its position as the fifth largest long-distance company in the United States.
The deal, enthusiastically received by Wall Street, will create a communications company with 6.3 million customers, a 100,000-mile fiber optic network and revenues of $2 billion.
After the announcement, Telco's stock shot up $6.75 to $28.75 in early trading on the Nasdaq market while Excel gained $2.50 to $21.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.

"This merger represents a significant strategic move for Excel as we continue to implement our vision of becoming a leading provider of communications products both domestically and internationally," Chairman Kenny A. Troutt said in a statement.

"Excel's access to the Telco network will also better position the combined company as it continues with its plans to enter the $100 billion local telephone market and ultimately provide a bundled package of local, long-distance and wireless services."
Telco offers discounted long-distance telephone services, primarily through two subscriber plans, Dial and Save and Long Distance Wholesale Club.
Dallas-based Excel said it estimated that it can realise cost savings in excess of $100 million in the first year after the merger is closed.
Under the terms of the agreement, Telco shareholders will receive 0.7595 share of common stock of the combined company and $15 in cash for each share of Telco common stock.
Based on Excel's trading price of $21.375, Telco shareholders will receive total compensation of about $31.23 a share, valuing the acquisition at $1.023 billion.
Excel shareholders will receive one share of the new company for each share of Excel common stock. Upon completion of the merger, Excel shareholders will own about 80 percent of the new company.
The transaction will be accounted for as a purchase, with the stock portion expected to be tax free to shareholders of both companies, Excel said.

Excel also said it obtained a $1 billion line of credit from an affiliate of Lehman Brothers, of which between $500 million and $600 million will be used to fund the cash portion of the merger and to refinance the existing indebtedness of Telco.
The merger agreement, unanimously approved by the board of directors of both companies, is expected to close by the end of the year.
Shareholders who hold a majority of the outstanding common stock of each company have agreed to vote in favour of the merger.
The announcement said the current Telco management team will remain in place and Telco will keep its headquarters in Chantilly, Va.

In a separate announcement, Excel said that its board of directors has increased the number of shares authorised to be repurchased under its previously-announced stock repurchase plan from 2 million to 10 million.
